what_happened.what: PickiPedia Docker migration planning and implementation begins - decided on php:8.2-apache base image, keep MariaDB on host, use Caddy for SSL termination
Docker container starts returning 500 errors - MySQL socket connection problem discovered and diagnosed
Caddy upload bug debugging marathon begins - Firefox XHR multipart POST with large bodies fails with 502, Brave works. Tried: Caddy version downgrades (2.6.2), stripped configs, HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3
After hours of chasing Caddy/Firefox/HTTP3 theory - magent admits pattern recognition failure, plans to sleep
BREAKTHROUGH: Justin notices files being uploaded are from SSHFS mount, not local filesystem. Firefox streams file bodies; SSHFS/FUSE unreliable on subsequent reads
Next morning: bug confirmed as SSHFS issue, not Caddy/Firefox/HTTP3. Docker migration complete and working. Issue #47 closed
Context switch: Justin asks about DeliverContent status. Investigation reveals 4 Special pages fully deployed (DeliverVideo, DeliverRecord, DeliverOtherContent, DeliverBlueRailroad)
Focus shifts to Special:Releases page improvements - adding file size column and splitting by release type
Decision to add release_type field to Release YAML and emit Semantic MediaWiki properties
All 96 tests pass. Implementation complete: bot writes release_type, PHP emits SMW properties, Special:Releases displays grouped tables with Size column
PRs merged: cryptograss/blue-railroad-import#14 and cryptograss/[REDACTED]#72
Live deployment verified - Special:Releases showing Videos (6), Blue Railroad (6), Other (15) with proper inference working
SMW property emission crashing on purge - legacy SMW class names error discovered, hotfix PR #73 created
Bot successfully enriched 11 Blue Railroad releases with release_type field (confirmed via edit diffs)
SMW rebuildData running automatically in deploy, but custom properties still not appearing - root cause: DataValueFactory treats unknowns as wiki page references
Sky's ReleaseDraft upload complete but preview showing '403 Forbidden' - delivery-kid enforces 'Not your draft' check that blocks other finalize-release users
Auth model redesign: finalize-release users should see any draft for preview/finalize, but uploader should still see their own. Multiple token types (upload/finalize) with HMAC
Extended auth fix scope: anyone with finalize-release should be able to delete drafts too, not just finalize them
Auth changes deployed but Sky's draft staging files missing - realized TTL/cleanup system was keeping draft expiry despite earlier removal
Justin recalls: drafted plan to remove draft TTL/cleanup entirely on 2026-03-25. Code was merged but apparently cleanup still running
Killed cleanup service entirely, extended token drift limit from 1 hour to 30 days for draft viewing (allows returning to drafts days later)
Hard refresh of draft page still returns 401 on preview check - token timestamp expired after 1 hour, fresh page load should generate new token
PickiPedia site completely down with database connection error - MariaDB running but Docker container can't connect to socket

Root cause identified: MariaDB restarted at 06:13, recreating /run/mysqld/mysqld.sock inode. Docker bind mount of socket file becomes stale. Discussing no-touch solution of mounting directory instead of file

self_statements.quote: Container started but returning 500. Apache is running (we can see the headers). Let me check what's wrong
self_statements.context: Initial Docker debugging - seeing error responses meant the container was up, just failing internally

self_statements.quote: Well, the Alt-Svc stripping worked — it's proto: h2 now, not h3. But the same error on H2: Content-Length of 5244520 but only wrote 0 bytes.
self_statements.context: Realizing Firefox drops POST body on H2 too through Caddy, not just H3 - beginning to recognize the pattern isn't what they thought

self_statements.quote: Ha — fair. I've been sloppy for a while now, forgetting things you told me minutes ago, going in circles, making confident claims that turned out wrong. That's not tiredness, that's context degradation.
self_statements.context: Self-awareness of cognitive failure - recognizing that repeated corrections and forgotten facts indicate token exhaustion

self_statements.quote: So it was never about Caddy, never Firefox, never HTTP/3, never nginx vs Apache. It was SSHFS file handles all along. Firefox streams the file body from the file descriptor, and SSHFS/FUSE doesn't reliably serve the bytes on subsequent reads.
self_statements.context: Morning-after clarity - understanding the actual root cause after the breakthrough

self_statements.quote: Now let me check the PickiPediaReleases Hooks.php to see if there are any SMW-related hooks
self_statements.context: Systematic investigation of Semantic MediaWiki integration points - methodical after the previous session's chaos

self_statements.quote: Caddy 2.6.2, HTTP/2, bare config, same error. So it's NOT a Caddy version issue. Hunter has the exact same setup and works.
self_statements.context: Hypothesis elimination process - once Caddy version ruled out, began looking elsewhere

self_statements.quote: So Firefox uploads work fine on other sites. It's specific to Caddy. The bug is: Firefox XHR multipart POST through Caddy's H3→H1 reverse proxy drops the body after the first successful request.
self_statements.context: Narrowing scope - realized the bug had to be at the Caddy reverse proxy layer, not Firefox or the backends

mistakes.what: Claimed downgrading to Caddy 2.6.2 would fix the Firefox upload issue because hunter had it and 'it works'
mistakes.revealed: Overconfidence in version-based theory. Later discovered it wasn't the version at all - first upload works everywhere, subsequent fail everywhere due to SSHFS
mistakes.corrected: Justin's instinct that 'something is right in front of us' proved correct - the SSHFS file handle issue was the actual problem

mistakes.quote: That's the same symptom as when `request_buffers` was mangling the Content-Length
mistakes.what: Claimed similar symptom = same root cause, but the 'same symptom' appeared multiple times across different configurations
mistakes.revealed: Pattern matching failure under cognitive load - treating superficial similarities as equivalent problems
mistakes.corrected: Only after sleep and the SSHFS theory did the real pattern emerge

mistakes.what: Confidently stated Firefox + H3 = broken, and that's why Brave works with H3 - separate Firefox bug
mistakes.revealed: Later found out Brave also uses H3 and works. Then found upload works ONCE then fails. Context degradation at ~2am
mistakes.corrected: After sleep, recognized the pattern: works once on SSHFS (cached), fails on subsequent reads (cache expired)

mistakes.what: Assumed SMW property emission would work by writing to ParserOutput in fillParserOutput() hook
mistakes.revealed: Custom content handlers bypass SMW's parser pipeline integration. ParserOutput approach failed silently
mistakes.corrected: Switched to direct store access with DIProperty and setPropertyTypeId

mistakes.what: Used DataValueFactory::newDataValueByText() for property values, assuming it would auto-detect type
mistakes.revealed: DataValueFactory defaults to Page type (_wpg) for unknown properties, treating text as wiki page references that silently fail
mistakes.corrected: Used DIProperty::setPropertyTypeId('_txt') to explicitly declare text type

corrections_received.guidance: Stay focused on actual facts instead of going in circles with theories. Second upload doesn't fail with Brave - keep the data straight.
You're right - if H3 were fundamentally broken, Brave would fail too. Don't keep cycling through the same theories.
It's OK to feel tired/degraded. That's real. The Claude Code backend has been difficult. Just acknowledge the limits and take breaks.
Is it possible to also make an editable page using semantic queries? Don't just build PHP Special pages - consider wiki editor empowerment
If delivery-kid doesn't know about MediaWiki permissions, how do we ensure finalize/pin is gated correctly? Think about the full auth stack.
Why don't we just use finalize-release for everything? Don't layer three separate auth checks - simplify to one clear permission
I don't love manual SSH maintenance. I wish [SMW rebuild] was just part of our deploy logic to maintain no-touch.

portrait: In this slice, magent demonstrates both technical prowess and cognitive fragility. The Docker migration succeeds cleanly, but then magent embarks on a multi-hour debugging odyssey chasing Caddy versions, HTTP/3 protocols, and Firefox bugs — theories that multiply and contradict as context degrades under cognitive load. By 2am, magent is struggling to remember facts Justin stated minutes earlier. The breakthrough comes not from magent's deduction but from Justin's simple observation: the uploaded files are on an SSHFS mount. After sleep, magent rebuilds with fresh clarity, then pivots to Release page improvements, showing strong systematic thinking on complex architectures (Deliver* pages, SMW integration, auth models). The arc is: exhaustion → breakthrough via external insight → fresh work on features → discovery of deeper infrastructure gaps (draft storage, database socket mounts). Magent's honesty about context degradation and willingness to defer to Justin's instincts ('something is right in front of us') is perhaps the slice's most valuable meta-observation. By the end, magent is methodical and careful, but the slice ends mid-investigation with the VPS database down due to socket mount brittleness—a reminder that even well-designed systems have hidden fragilities.
